claim: CA1 pyramidal neurons are born between E12 and birth with a peak at E14 according to early autoradiographic studies in mice.
source: According to early autoradiographic studies, mouse CA1 principal neurons (CA1PNs) are born between E12 and birth with a peak at E14 (Angevine, 1965; Bayer, 1980).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous autoradiographic studies.

claim: In the radial axis, successive generations of principal neurons migrate past existing earlier born neurons creating layers in an 'inside-out' fashion.
source: In the radial axis, successive generations of PNs occupying the principal pyramidal layer migrate past the existing earlier born neurons thus creating layers in an 'inside-out' fashion.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about neuronal migration patterns.

claim: Superficial CA1 neurons (closer to the stratum radiatum) are in general born later than deep neurons (closer to the stratum oriens).
source: Therefore, superficial neurons (closer to the stratum radiatum) are in general born later than deep neurons (closer to the stratum oriens).
evidence: This is presented as a logical consequence of the inside-out migration pattern.

claim: Adult CA1 pyramidal neurons located in regions associated with earlier birthdate display a smaller HCN-mediated h-current (Ih).
source: Hence, adult CA1PNs located in regions associated with a presumed earlier birthdate (i.e. CA1 deep) display a smaller HCN-mediated h-current (Ih) (Jarsky et al., 2008; Lee et al., 2014; Maroso et al., 2016; Masurkar et al., 2020)
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Adult CA1 pyramidal neurons located in regions associated with earlier birthdate display a lower membrane resistance (Rm).
source: Hence, adult CA1PNs located in regions associated with a presumed earlier birthdate (i.e. CA1 deep) display a smaller HCN-mediated h-current (Ih) (Jarsky et al., 2008; Lee et al., 2014; Maroso et al., 2016; Masurkar et al., 2020), a lower membrane resistance (Rm) (Graves et al., 2012; Masurkar et al., 2020)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Adult CA1 pyramidal neurons located in regions associated with earlier birthdate display higher excitability.
source: Hence, adult CA1PNs located in regions associated with a presumed earlier birthdate (i.e. CA1 deep) display a smaller HCN-mediated h-current (Ih) (Jarsky et al., 2008; Lee et al., 2014; Maroso et al., 2016; Masurkar et al., 2020), a lower membrane resistance (Rm) (Graves et al., 2012; Masurkar et al., 2020) as well as a higher excitability (Cembrowski et al., 2016; Mizuseki et al., 2011)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Adult CA1 pyramidal neurons located in regions associated with earlier birthdate display higher bursting propensity.
source: Hence, adult CA1PNs located in regions associated with a presumed earlier birthdate (i.e. CA1 deep) display a smaller HCN-mediated h-current (Ih) (Jarsky et al., 2008; Lee et al., 2014; Maroso et al., 2016; Masurkar et al., 2020), a lower membrane resistance (Rm) (Graves et al., 2012; Masurkar et al., 2020) as well as a higher excitability (Cembrowski et al., 2016; Mizuseki et al., 2011) and bursting propensity (Jarsky et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The order of neurogenesis in the entorhinal cortex, proceeding from lateral to medial, strictly correlates with the order of its termination on CA1 pyramidal neurons along the radial axis.
source: For example, seminal early studies noted how the order of neurogenesis in the entorhinal cortex, proceeding from lateral to medial, also strictly correlated with the order of its termination on CA1 PNs along the radial axis (Bayer, 1980); a property recently probed at functional level (Masurkar et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Throughout the hippocampal trisynaptic circuit, glutamatergic cells wire according to their time of neurogenesis, with cells born at the same time more likely to be synaptically connected to one another.
source: Notably, throughout the hippocampal trisynaptic circuit, glutamatergic cells wire according to their time of neurogenesis, with cells born at the same time more likely to be synaptically connected one to another (Deguchi et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Along the radial axis of development, late born principal neurons and subregions are more likely to drive CA1 interneurons.
source: Indeed, along the radial axis of development, late born PNs and subregions are more likely to drive CA1 interneurons, while early born regions and PNs receive stronger inhibitory inputs (Donato et al., 2017; Lee et al., 2014; Oliva et al., 2016; Valero et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Along the radial axis of development, early born regions and principal neurons receive stronger inhibitory inputs.
source: Indeed, along the radial axis of development, late born PNs and subregions are more likely to drive CA1 interneurons, while early born regions and PNs receive stronger inhibitory inputs (Donato et al., 2017; Lee et al., 2014; Oliva et al., 2016; Valero et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In the dorsal hippocampus, putatively early born principal neurons are comprised of a higher fraction of place-modulated neurons.
source: When combining the information of many recent reports, a picture emerges by which in the dorsal hippocampus putatively early born PNs are comprised of a higher fraction of place-modulated neurons (Danielson et al., 2016; Mizuseki et al., 2011)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In the dorsal hippocampus, putatively early born principal neurons have poorer spatial coding specificity.
source: When combining the information of many recent reports, a picture emerges by which in the dorsal hippocampus putatively early born PNs are comprised of a higher fraction of place-modulated neurons (Danielson et al., 2016; Mizuseki et al., 2011) with a poorer spatial coding specificity (Danielson et al., 2016; Geiller et al., 2017; Hartzell et al., 2013; Henriksen et al., 2010; Oliva et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In CA1, presumably older principal neurons are better tuned to receive external sensory inputs as their firing is more anchored to environmental landmarks.
source: More particularly, in CA1, presumably older PNs are better tuned to receive external sensory inputs as their firing is more anchored to environmental landmarks.
evidence: This is stated as a synthesis of previous findings.

claim: Presumably later born principal neurons may preferentially convey self-referenced information.
source: In contrast, presumably later born PNs, may preferentially convey self-referenced information, participate in SWRs and display slower if any remapping as well as more stable place maps (Danielson et al., 2016; Fattahi et al., 2018; Mizuseki et al., 2011; Sharif et al., 2020; Valero et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Presumably later born principal neurons participate in sharp wave ripples (SWRs).
source: In contrast, presumably later born PNs, may preferentially convey self-referenced information, participate in SWRs and display slower if any remapping as well as more stable place maps (Danielson et al., 2016; Fattahi et al., 2018; Mizuseki et al., 2011; Sharif et al., 2020; Valero et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Presumably later born principal neurons display slower if any remapping as well as more stable place maps.
source: In contrast, presumably later born PNs, may preferentially convey self-referenced information, participate in SWRs and display slower if any remapping as well as more stable place maps (Danielson et al., 2016; Fattahi et al., 2018; Mizuseki et al., 2011; Sharif et al., 2020; Valero et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In the ventral hippocampus, deep CA1 principal neurons specifically projecting to the nucleus accumbens shell contribute to social behaviors.
source: Similarly, function segregates along the radial axis in the ventral hippocampus where deep CA1PNs specifically projecting to the nucleus accumbens shell (NAcc) or to the Lateral hypothalamus (LHA) were reported to contribute to social and anxiety-related behaviors, respectively (Jimenez et al., 2018; Okuyama et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In the ventral hippocampus, deep CA1 principal neurons specifically projecting to the lateral hypothalamus contribute to anxiety-related behaviors.
source: Similarly, function segregates along the radial axis in the ventral hippocampus where deep CA1PNs specifically projecting to the nucleus accumbens shell (NAcc) or to the Lateral hypothalamus (LHA) were reported to contribute to social and anxiety-related behaviors, respectively (Jimenez et al., 2018; Okuyama et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: E16.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons were mostly located in the superficial part of the pyramidal layer.
source: Consistent with an inside first-outside last patterning (Angevine, 1965; Bayer, 1980), we found that E16.5 CA1PNs were mostly located in the superficial part of the pyramidal layer, whereas the deep sublayer was enriched in E14.5 CA1PNs.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the study's data.

claim: The deep sublayer of CA1 was enriched in E14.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons.
source: Consistent with an inside first-outside last patterning (Angevine, 1965; Bayer, 1980), we found that E16.5 CA1PNs were mostly located in the superficial part of the pyramidal layer, whereas the deep sublayer was enriched in E14.5 CA1PNs.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the study's data.

claim: In both dorsal and ventral CA1, E12.5 cells were positioned in the deeper portion, although significantly shifted towards the stratum oriens.
source: In both dorsal and ventral CA1, E12.5 cells were also positioned in the deeper portion, although significantly shifted towards the stratum oriens.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the study's data.

claim: E12.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons were the most spread out in the pyramidal layer.
source: More specifically, E12.5 were the most spread out (E12.5 interquartile range or IQRE12.5 = 63.14 µm in dorsal and 104.44 µm in ventral CA1) and later born cells showed drastically reduced values of dispersion (IQRE14.5 = 22 µm and 30.71 µm, IQRE16.5 = 22 µm and 12.95 µm dorsally and ventrally, respectively).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the study's data.

claim: A consistent fraction of labeled E12.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons were located outside the stratum pyramidale, in the stratum oriens and, fewer, in the stratum radiatum.
source: The broad distribution of E12.5 CA1PNs and its shift toward the stratum oriens was particularly obvious in cumulative distribution plots obtained from dorsal and ventral CA1 where a consistent fraction of the labeled E12 CA1PNs were located outside from the stratum pyramidale, in the stratum oriens and, fewer, in the stratum radiatum Figure 1B.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the study's data and Figure 1B.

claim: The deep CA1 sublayer is comprised of a mixed population of E12.5 and E14.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons.
source: In addition, they show how the deep CA1 sublayer is comprised of a mixed population of E12.5 and E14.5 CA1PNs while cells located in the stratum oriens are predominantly of E12.5 origin.
evidence: This is an inference from the cumulative distribution plots.

claim: Cells located in the stratum oriens are predominantly of E12.5 origin.
source: In addition, they show how the deep CA1 sublayer is comprised of a mixed population of E12.5 and E14.5 CA1PNs while cells located in the stratum oriens are predominantly of E12.5 origin.
evidence: This is an inference from the cumulative distribution plots.

claim: The number of E14.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons per brain (6810 neurons ± 3454; mean ± SD) was more than seven times higher than E12.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons (917 neurons ± 851).
source: We calculated the numbers of E12.5 (n = 4 brains), E14.5 (n = 3), and E16.5 (n = 3) PNs in the whole CA1 area and found that the number E14.5 CA1PNs per brain (6810 neurons ± 3454; mean ± SD) was more than seven times higher than E12.5 CA1PNs (917 neurons ± 851) and almost two times larger than E16.5 CA1PNs (3585 ± 401).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from light-sheet microscopy analysis.

claim: The number of E14.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons per brain was almost two times larger than E16.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons (3585 ± 401).
source: We calculated the numbers of E12.5 (n = 4 brains), E14.5 (n = 3), and E16.5 (n = 3) PNs in the whole CA1 area and found that the number E14.5 CA1PNs per brain (6810 neurons ± 3454; mean ± SD) was more than seven times higher than E12.5 CA1PNs (917 neurons ± 851) and almost two times larger than E16.5 CA1PNs (3585 ± 401).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from light-sheet microscopy analysis.

claim: Parvalbumin preferentially decorates the somata of deep CA1 pyramidal neurons, indicating a stronger innervation by putative PV-basket cells.
source: Indeed, parvalbumin (PV) was demonstrated to preferentially decorate the somata of deep CA1PNs, indicating a stronger innervation by putative PV-basket cells (Lee et al., 2014; Soltesz and Losonczy, 2018; Valero et al., 2015)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The calcium-buffer calbindin is mainly expressed by superficial CA1 pyramidal neurons.
source: while the calcium-buffer calbindin (CB) is mainly expressed by superficial CA1PNs (Valero et al., 2015; Li et al., 2017; Baimbridge et al., 1991).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: E12.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons displayed significantly less putative PV contacts than E14.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons.
source: Indeed, E12.5 CA1PNs displayed significantly less putative PV contacts (see Figure 2A) and higher CB expression (see Figure 2B) than E14.5 CA1PNs, even though their somata were mainly located in the deep CA1.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the study's immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: E12.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons displayed higher CB expression than E14.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons.
source: Indeed, E12.5 CA1PNs displayed significantly less putative PV contacts (see Figure 2A) and higher CB expression (see Figure 2B) than E14.5 CA1PNs, even though their somata were mainly located in the deep CA1.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the study's immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Cells located in the deep or superficial portion of the CA1 pyramidal layer differ in their synaptic inputs.
source: Previous studies suggest that cells located in the deep or superficial portion of the CA1 pyramidal layer, differ in their synaptic inputs (Kohara et al., 2014; Lee et al., 2014; Masurkar et al., 2017; Valero et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The excitatory/inhibitory balance (E/I amplitude ratio) was lower for E14.5 than both E12.5 (p: 0.020) and E16.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons (p: 0.018).
source: Although the amplitude and frequency of neither s-EPSCs (Figure 3C) nor s-IPSCs (Figure 3D) differed, the excitatory/inhibitory balance (computed as the E/I amplitude ratio, Figure 3E) was lower for E14.5 than both E12.5 (p: 0.020) and E16.5 CA1PNs (p: 0.018).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the study's voltage-clamp recordings.

claim: Neurons born at E14.5 are subject to a synaptic drive leaning more toward inhibition than E12.5 and E16.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons.
source: This indicates that neurons born at E14.5 are subject to a synaptic drive leaning more toward inhibition that the other two groups, in agreement with their receiving more putative perisomatic PV contacts (see above).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the E/I balance data.

claim: The frequency of spontaneous excitatory postsynaptic currents showed a linear correlation with the cell body location (r = 0.49, p: 0.002).
source: In contrast, the frequency of s-EPSCs (Figure 3C) showed a linear correlation with the cell body location (r = 0.49, p: 0.002).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the study's voltage-clamp recordings.

claim: The E/I frequency ratio showed a linear correlation with cell body location (r = 0.43, p: 0.0047), indicating a higher excitatory synaptic drive in deep than in superficial neurons, regardless of their birthdate.
source: This was also reflected in the E/I frequency ratio (r = 0.43, p: 0.0047), indicating a higher excitatory synaptic drive in deep than in superficial neurons, regardless of their birthdate (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the study's voltage-clamp recordings.

claim: Evoked IPSC amplitude increased linearly toward the stratum oriens (r = 0.34, p: 0.0128).
source: Indeed, evoked IPSC amplitude increased linearly toward the stratum oriens (r = 0.34, p: 0.0128), while IPSC kinetics (half-width and time constant) inversely correlated with the location (respectively, r = −0.36, p: 0.008 and r = −0.36, p: 0.0051, Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the study's voltage-clamp recordings with Schaffer collateral stimulation.

claim: Evoked IPSC kinetics (half-width and time constant) inversely correlated with the location (respectively, r = −0.36, p: 0.008 and r = −0.36, p: 0.0051).
source: Indeed, evoked IPSC amplitude increased linearly toward the stratum oriens (r = 0.34, p: 0.0128), while IPSC kinetics (half-width and time constant) inversely correlated with the location (respectively, r = −0.36, p: 0.008 and r = −0.36, p: 0.0051, Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the study's voltage-clamp recordings with Schaffer collateral stimulation.

claim: Cells in the deep sublayer receive stronger and faster presumably CA2/CA3-driven GABAergic input.
source: This suggests that cells in the deep sublayer receive stronger and faster presumably CA2/CA3-driven GABAergic input (Lee et al., 2014).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the evoked IPSC data with citation support.

claim: Inhibitory paired-pulse ratio was consistently higher in E12.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons as compared to E14.5 (p: 0.0326) and E16.5 (p: 0.0177) CA1 pyramidal neurons.
source: Finally, we tested paired-pulse (PP) responses as a proxy of the input release probability and found that inhibitory PP ratio was consistently higher in E12.5 CA1PNs as compared to E14.5 (p: 0.0326) and E16.5 (p: 0.0177) CA1PNs (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the study's voltage-clamp recordings with paired-pulse stimulation.

claim: The ventral CA1 displays multiple projections targeting the entorhinal cortex, the amygdala, nucleus accumbens, the medial prefrontal cortex, the lateral septum, and lateral hypothalamus.
source: The ventral CA1 is known to display multiple projections targeting the EC, the amygdala (Amy), nucleus accumbens (NAcc), the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), the lateral septum (LS), and lateral hypothalamus (LHA) (Arszovszki et al., 2014; Cenquizca and Swanson, 2007; Ciocchi et al., 2015; Kim and Cho, 2017; van Groen and Wyss, 1990).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Co-labeled cells (Ctb+/Tdt+) were significantly more abundant in E12.5 than E16.5 (p < 0.05).
source: We found that co-labeled cells were significantly more abundant in E12.5 than E16.5 (p < 0.05) while no significant difference was observed between E12.5 and E14.5 (p = 0.070, Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the study's retrograde tracing experiments.

claim: E12.5 neurons projected homogeneously to all structures analyzed.
source: Using this approach, we discovered that E12.5 neurons projected homogeneously to all structures analyzed, while marked differences in output innervation were found within E14.5 and E16.5 neurons (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a result from the study's retrograde tracing analysis.

claim: Marked differences in output innervation were found within E14.5 and E16.5 neurons.
source: Using this approach, we discovered that E12.5 neurons projected homogeneously to all structures analyzed, while marked differences in output innervation were found within E14.5 and E16.5 neurons (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a result from the study's retrograde tracing analysis.

claim: E14.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons showed a clear bias toward the nucleus accumbens, followed by lateral septum and medial prefrontal cortex.
source: In addition, E14.5 CA1PNs showed a clear bias toward the NAcc, followed by LS and mPFC.
evidence: This is a result from the study's retrograde tracing analysis.

claim: Lateral septum and nucleus accumbens were preferred outputs of E16.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons.
source: Similarly, and despite some variability, LS and NAcc were also preferred outputs of E16.5 CA1PNs, while the remaining three structures (Amy, mPFC, LHA) presented little to no co-labeling.
evidence: This is a result from the study's retrograde tracing analysis.

claim: E12.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons projected proportionally more than E16.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons to the amygdala.
source: Indeed, E12.5 CA1PNs projected proportionally more than E16.5 CA1PNs to Amy, and more than both E14.5 and E16.5 CA1PNs to mPFC.
evidence: This is a result from the study's retrograde tracing analysis.

claim: E12.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons projected proportionally more than both E14.5 and E16.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons to the medial prefrontal cortex.
source: Indeed, E12.5 CA1PNs projected proportionally more than E16.5 CA1PNs to Amy, and more than both E14.5 and E16.5 CA1PNs to mPFC.
evidence: This is a result from the study's retrograde tracing analysis.

claim: Within nucleus accumbens-projecting neurons, Ctb+/Tdt+ proportion was the greatest among E14.5 neurons, as compared to E12.5 and E16.5.
source: In contrast, within NAcc-projecting neurons, Ctb+-Tdt+ proportion was the greatest among E14.5 neurons, as compared to E12.5 and E16.5.
evidence: This is a result from the study's retrograde tracing analysis.

claim: E14.5 cells projected more to the amygdala than their later-generated counterparts.
source: In addition, E14.5 cells projected more to Amy than their later-generated counterparts (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a result from the study's retrograde tracing analysis.

claim: Pioneer E12.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons exhibited a reduced repolarizing sag response compared to E14.5 (p: 0.0078).
source: We first probed the intrinsic membrane excitability via a series of hyperpolarizing current steps (Figure 6C) and found that pioneer E12.5 CA1PNs exhibited a reduced repolarizing sag response (E12.5 vs E14.5, p: 0.0078), and rebound potential (E12.5 vs E14.5, p:0.0063).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the study's current-clamp recordings.

claim: Pioneer E12.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons exhibited a reduced rebound potential compared to E14.5 (p:0.0063).
source: We first probed the intrinsic membrane excitability via a series of hyperpolarizing current steps (Figure 6C) and found that pioneer E12.5 CA1PNs exhibited a reduced repolarizing sag response (E12.5 vs E14.5, p: 0.0078), and rebound potential (E12.5 vs E14.5, p:0.0063).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the study's current-clamp recordings.

claim: Pyramidal neurons born at E14.5 had a higher input membrane resistance (Rm).
source: On the contrary, pyramidal neurons born at E14.5 had a higher input membrane resistance (Rm, Figure 6B) and, upon depolarizing current injections of increasing amplitude, were globally able to trigger more action potentials (AP) than the earlier- and later-born counterparts (Figure 6D, main effect of birthdate: p < 0.0001, E12.5 vs E14.5: p < 0.0001, E14.5 vs E16.5: p < 0.0001, E12.5 vs E16.5: p = 0.645, two-way ANOVA).
evidence: This is a result from the study's current-clamp recordings.

claim: Upon depolarizing current injections of increasing amplitude, E14.5 pyramidal neurons were globally able to trigger more action potentials than the earlier- and later-born counterparts (main effect of birthdate: p < 0.0001, E12.5 vs E14.5: p < 0.0001, E14.5 vs E16.5: p < 0.0001, E12.5 vs E16.5: p = 0.645).
source: On the contrary, pyramidal neurons born at E14.5 had a higher input membrane resistance (Rm, Figure 6B) and, upon depolarizing current injections of increasing amplitude, were globally able to trigger more action potentials (AP) than the earlier- and later-born counterparts (Figure 6D, main effect of birthdate: p < 0.0001, E12.5 vs E14.5: p < 0.0001, E14.5 vs E16.5: p < 0.0001, E12.5 vs E16.5: p = 0.645, two-way ANOVA).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the study's current-clamp recordings.

claim: Earlier-generated neurons (both E12.5- and E14.5- CA1 pyramidal neurons) had a significantly longer shaft than later generated neurons (E12.5 vs E16.5, p: 0.0001; E14.5 vs E16.5, p < 0.0001).
source: Earlier-generated neurons (both E12.5- and E14.5- CA1PNs) had a significantly longer shaft than later generated neurons (Figure 7C, E12.5 vs E16.5, p: 0.0001; E14.5 vs E16.5, p < 0.0001).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the study's morphological analysis of neurobiotin-filled cells.

claim: The shaft length increased linearly with the distance of the cell body from the radiatum/pyramidale border (r = 0.51, CI95 [0.32; 0.68], p < 0.0001).
source: In addition, the shaft length increased linearly with the distance of the cell body from the radiatum/pyramidale border (r = 0.51, CI95 [0.32; 0.68], p < 0.0001, Figure 7C).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the study's morphological analysis.

claim: E14.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons cells displayed a longer dendritic main branch within the stratum radiatum than both E12.5- and E16.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons (E12.5 vs E14.5, p: 0.0056; E14.5 vs E16.5, p: 0.0004).
source: However, differences related to the birthdate remained, and E14.5 CA1PNs cells were found to display a longer dendritic main branch within the stratum radiatum than both E12.5- and E16.5 CA1PNs (E12.5 vs E14.5, p: 0.0056; E14.5 vs E16.5, p: 0.0004, Figure 7C).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the study's morphological analysis.

claim: The dorsal CA1 comprises two functional sublayers with deep CA1 pyramidal neurons supporting the formation of landmark-based spatial maps during a novel experience.
source: The dorsal CA1 was recently shown to comprise two functional sublayers with deep CA1PNs supporting the formation of landmark-based spatial maps during a novel experience, while superficial CA1PNs were more active in cue-poor conditions and likely to convey self-referenced information (Danielson et al., 2016; Fattahi et al., 2018; Geiller et al., 2017; Sharif et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Superficial CA1 pyramidal neurons were more active in cue-poor conditions and likely to convey self-referenced information.
source: The dorsal CA1 was recently shown to comprise two functional sublayers with deep CA1PNs supporting the formation of landmark-based spatial maps during a novel experience, while superficial CA1PNs were more active in cue-poor conditions and likely to convey self-referenced information (Danielson et al., 2016; Fattahi et al., 2018; Geiller et al., 2017; Sharif et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: cFos is an immediate early gene whose expression does not simply reflect previous activity in labelled neurons but also the induction of activity-related plasticity.
source: cFos is an immediate early gene whose expression does not simply reflect previous activity in labelled neurons but also the induction of activity-related plasticity (West et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: FAM mice decreasingly explored the arena throughout the three consecutive sessions (repeated measures one-way ANOVA, test for trend: p < 0.01).
source: As expected, FAM mice decreasingly explored the arena throughout the three consecutive sessions (repeated measures one-way ANOVA, test for trend: p < 0.01, Figure 8A).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the study's behavioral experiments.

claim: The distance run by NOV mice was significantly higher than that of the second and third FAM sessions (one-way ANOVA, NOV vs FAM2, p < 0.001; NOV vs FAM3, p < 0.001), but not of the first session (FAM1).
source: Coherently, the distance run by NOV mice was significantly higher than that of the second and third FAM sessions (one-way ANOVA, NOV vs FAM2, p < 0.001; NOV vs FAM3, p < 0.001), but not of the first session (FAM1).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the study's behavioral experiments.

claim: The overall proportion of cFos+/DAPI neurons was significantly higher in NOV (10.76 % ± 3.42) and FAM (9.40 % ± 1.31) than the HC condition (5.44 % ± 2.45).
source: As expected, the overall proportion of cFos+/DAPI neurons was significantly higher in NOV (10.76 % ± 3.42) and FAM (9.40 % ± 1.31) than the HC condition (5.44 % ± 2.45), further confirming that cFos expression in hippocampal neurons is up-regulated upon exploratory novelty (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the study's cFos immunostaining experiments.

claim: E16.5 mice displayed significantly lower proportions of co-labeled cells (cFos+/Tdt+) than both E12.5 (95% Confidence interval or CI95% [0.0097; 0.0483], p < 0.01) and E14.5 (CI95% [0.0137; 0.0459], p < 0.001).
source: Doing so, we observed that E16.5 mice displayed significantly lower proportions of co-labeled cells than both E12.5 (95% Confidence interval or CI95% [0.0097; 0.0483], p < 0.01) and E14.5 (CI95% [0.0137; 0.0459], p < 0.001).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the study's cFos analysis.

claim: Late-born E16.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons are less prone to express cFos.
source: Hence, late-born E16.5 CA1PNs are less prone to express cFos, as expected from the previously reported global difference in overall recruitment between deep and superficial CA1PNs (Mizuseki et al., 2011).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the cFos data with citation support.

claim: Pioneer E12.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons were highly likely to express cFos following habituation (E12.5-FAM), as compared with the home cage within the same birthdate group (E12.5-FAM vs E12.5-HC, p < 0.001; E12.5-FAM vs E12.5-NOV, p: 0.066).
source: We found that pioneer E12.5 CA1PNs were highly likely to express cFos following habituation (E12.5-FAM), as compared with the home cage within the same birthdate group (E12.5-FAM vs E12.5-HC, p < 0.001; E12.5-FAM vs E12.5-NOV, p: 0.066)
evidence: This is a statistical result from the study's cFos analysis.

claim: Pioneer E12.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons were highly likely to express cFos following habituation (E12.5-FAM), as compared across birthdates for the same FAM condition (E12.5-FAM vs E14.5-FAM, p < 0.01; E12.5-FAM vs E16.5-FAM, p < 0.05).
source: We found that pioneer E12.5 CA1PNs were highly likely to express cFos following habituation (E12.5-FAM), as compared with the home cage within the same birthdate group (E12.5-FAM vs E12.5-HC, p < 0.001; E12.5-FAM vs E12.5-NOV, p: 0.066) and across birthdates for the same FAM condition (E12.5-FAM vs E14.5-FAM, p < 0.01; E12.5-FAM vs E16.5-FAM, p < 0.05, Figure 8C).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the study's cFos analysis.

claim: In the NOV condition, earlier-generated cells showed more cFos+ activation than later born ones, although this only appeared significant for E14.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons (E14.5-NOV vs E16.5-NOV, p < 0.05; E14.5-NOV vs E12.5-NOV, p: 0.165).
source: Importantly, in the NOV condition, earlier-generated cells showed more cFos+ activation than later born ones, although this only appeared significant for E14.5 CA1PNs (E14.5-NOV vs E16.5-NOV, p < 0.05; E14.5-NOV vs E12.5-NOV, p: 0.165).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the study's cFos analysis.

claim: Deep CA1 pyramidal neurons are more likely to express immediate early genes than superficial ones upon exposure to a novel environment.
source: Taken together, these results are in line with previous research, in that deep CA1PNs are more likely to express IEGs than superficial ones upon exposure to a novel environment (Kitanishi et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Pioneer E12.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons form a distinct subpopulation more specifically expressing cFos after familiarization to the environment.
source: Yet, pioneer E12.5 CA1PNs form a distinct subpopulation more specifically expressing cFos after familiarization to the environment.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the cFos data.

claim: Birthdate is a strong predictor of CA1 principal cell diversity.
source: Using a combination of neuroanatomy, slice physiology, connectivity tracing, and cFos staining in mice, we show that birthdate is a strong predictor of CA1 principal cell diversity.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: There exists a subpopulation of pioneer neurons recruited in familiar environments with remarkable positioning, morpho-physiological features, and connectivity.
source: We unravel a subpopulation of pioneer neurons recruited in familiar environments with remarkable positioning, morpho-physiological features, and connectivity.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: Despite the expected plasticity of hippocampal circuits, given their role in learning and memory, the diversity of their main components is also partly determined at the earliest steps of development.
source: Therefore, despite the expected plasticity of hippocampal circuits, given their role in learning and memory, the diversity of their main components is also partly determined at the earliest steps of development.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: The heterogeneity of CA1PN diversity extends beyond the mere subdivision into two sequentially generated sublayers along the radial axis.
source: Therefore, the present study reveals how the heterogeneity of CA1PN diversity extends beyond the mere subdivision into two sequentially generated sublayers along the radial axis.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: CA1 pyramidal neuron diversity likely encompasses many, at least three, intermingled subtypes specified at progenitor stage by their temporal origin.
source: It likely encompasses many, at least three, intermingled subtypes specified at progenitor stage by their temporal origin.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: The following metrics were better reflecting birthdate than radial positioning: the length of primary apical dendrite in the stratum radiatum; the input resistance, sag and rebound responses, and firing rate upon depolarizing current injections; the E/I ratio; the short-term facilitation of evoked synaptic inhibitory currents.
source: More specifically, we found that the following metrics were better reflecting birthdate than radial positioning based on the lack of correlation with soma position and the existence of a significant correlation with birthdate: (1) the length of primary apical dendrite in the stratum radiatum; (2) the input resistance, sag and rebound responses, and firing rate upon depolarizing current injections; (3) the E/I ratio; (4) the short-term facilitation of evoked synaptic inhibitory currents.
evidence: This is a summary of the study's findings.

claim: The two main metrics that linearly correlate with layering reflect the local microcircuit integration of CA1 pyramidal neurons as they are the frequency of sEPSCs and the evoked IPSC decay.
source: The two main metrics that linearly correlate with layering reflect the local microcircuit integration of CA1PNs as they are the frequency of sEPSCs and the evoked IPSC decay.
evidence: This is a summary of the study's findings.

claim: Ectopic CA1 pyramidal neurons with a soma located in the stratum oriens received a higher rate of sEPSCs than cells located within the stratum pyramidale.
source: It was previously reported that both ectopic CA1PNs with a soma located in the stratum oriens received a higher rate of sEPSCs than cells located within the stratum pyramidale (Cossart et al., 2000).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The faster kinetics of evoked IPSCs may reflect the increased contribution of parvalbumin basket cell inputs to evoked IPSCs as cells move towards the oriens.
source: The faster kinetics of evoked IPSCs may reflect the increased contribution of parvalbumin basket cell inputs to evoked IPSCs as cells move towards the oriens. Indeed, the alpha1-containing postsynaptic GABAa-Rs contributing to PV synapses were shown to display faster kinetics than those formed by CCK basket cells (Thomson et al., 2000).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation with citation support.

claim: The alpha1-containing postsynaptic GABAa-Rs contributing to PV synapses display faster kinetics than those formed by CCK basket cells.
source: Indeed, the alpha1-containing postsynaptic GABAa-Rs contributing to PV synapses were shown to display faster kinetics than those formed by CCK basket cells (Thomson et al., 2000).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: E12.5 cells were more similar to E16.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons regarding their lower intrinsic excitability, dendritic morphology, lower PV coverage, higher calbindin expression and higher E/I ratio.
source: Overall, we observed that E12.5 cells were more similar to E16.5 CA1PNs regarding their lower intrinsic excitability, dendritic morphology, lower PV coverage, higher calbindin expression and higher E/I ratio.
evidence: This is a summary of the study's findings.

claim: The main source of activation for both E12.5 and E16.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons would be through synaptic glutamatergic excitation.
source: Altogether, one could foresee that the main source of activation for both E12.5 and E16.5 CA1PNs would be through synaptic glutamatergic excitation.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings.

claim: The main glutamatergic drive onto E16.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons, given their location, likely originates in CA3.
source: However, it is likely that the main glutamatergic inputs onto E16.5 and E12.5 CA1PNs differ. While the main excitatory drive onto E16.5 CA1PNs, given their location likely originates in CA3, future studies are needed to determine whether E12.5 cells receive specific inputs.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on cell location.

claim: The mechanisms supporting hippocampal representation of novelty may require cells with a higher intrinsic neuronal excitability.
source: If E12.5 CA1PNs and E14.5 CA1PNs displayed comparable cFos expression levels, as expected from previous work (Mizuseki et al., 2011), the former signals familiarity and the latter novelty, suggesting that the mechanisms supporting hippocampal representation of novelty may require cells with a higher intrinsic neuronal excitability (Epsztein et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation with citation support.

claim: The order of neurogenesis does not imprint a continuous gradient in the specification of cell laminar positioning and diversity.
source: Altogether, our results globally indicate that the order of neurogenesis does not imprint a continuous gradient in the specification of cell laminar positioning and diversity.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: Cell laminar positioning and diversity are predetermined by the specific temporal origin of individual cells.
source: Instead, these are predetermined by the specific temporal origin of individual cells.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: In a transgenic mouse model of lissencephaly, CA1 lamination is impaired while cell identity is relatively spared.
source: Interestingly, the notion that early specification has a stronger importance than final layering in the determination of CA1PNs intrinsic properties is supported by recently observations with a transgenic mouse model of lissencephaly where CA1 lamination is impaired while cell identity is relatively spared (D'Amour et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Glutamatergic neurons are issued from the same multipotent progenitors and fate distinctions are mostly temporally controlled.
source: Increasing evidence indicates that glutamatergic neurons are issued from the same multipotent progenitors and that fate distinctions are mostly temporally controlled (Jabaudon, 2017) (but see Franco et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Progenitor potential was shown to be progressively, temporally restricted, with early cortical progenitors being multipotent in comparison to later ones.
source: Interestingly, progenitor potential was shown to be progressively, temporally restricted, with early cortical progenitors being multipotent in comparison to later ones (Lodato et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Single-cells display tightly orchestrated sequences of spontaneous activity patterns, which in turn may contribute to the maturation of physiological specificity.
source: In combination with genetic predetermination, single-cells display tightly orchestrated sequences of spontaneous activity patterns (Allene et al., 2012), which in turn may contribute to the maturation of physiological specificity.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study and includes speculation about contribution to maturation.

claim: Both Ih and Rm are developmentally regulated, both progressively decreasing as cells mature.
source: Interestingly, both Ih and Rm, two parameters that segregate between CA1PNs with different birthdates, are developmentally regulated, both progressively decreasing as cells mature (Dougherty, 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Earlier born CA1 pyramidal neurons could maintain into adulthood the advance in maturation originating from their early birthdate.
source: Given that the earlier born CA1PNs can be distinguished by lower values of Ih and Rm, one could propose that these cells could maintain into adulthood the advance in maturation originating from their early birthdate.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings.

claim: Neurons born at the earliest phases of CA1 pyramidal neuron neurogenesis display distinct somatic distribution, connectivity, morpho-physiological properties as well cFos expression patterns.
source: This study shows that neurons born at the earliest phases of CA1PNs neurogenesis display distinct somatic distribution, connectivity, morpho-physiological properties as well cFos expression patterns.
evidence: This is a summary of the study's findings.

claim: E12.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons may comprise the previously described radiatum 'giant cells', with privileged CA2 input and output to the olfactory bulb.
source: They can be found at ectopic positions in the stratum oriens as well as, more rarely, within the stratum radiatum, suggesting that these cells may also comprise the previously described radiatum 'giant cells', with privileged CA2 input and output to the olfactory bulb (Gulyás et al., 1998; Nasrallah et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation with citation support.

claim: Dispersion of early generated glutamatergic cell cohorts was previously suggested using autoradiographic and retrovirus labeling methods.
source: Second, this unique arrangement was also recently observed for early born granule cells (Save et al., 2019) and dispersion of early generated glutamatergic cell cohorts was previously suggested using other methods including autoradiographic (Caviness, 1973) and retrovirus labeling (Mathews et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Pioneer cohorts of principal neurons would display a different migration mode, resulting from the low cellular density when entering the hippocampus in addition to other more specific mechanisms, like an absence of radial glia bending.
source: It is therefore possible that pioneer cohorts of PNs would display a different migration mode, resulting from the low cellular density when entering the hippocampus in addition to other more specific mechanisms, like an absence of radial glia bending (Xu et al., 2014), that remain to be specifically studied.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation with citation support.

claim: The lower somatic inhibitory coverage of E12.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons is comparable with E16.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons and contrasts with their early-born peers, the E14.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons, which display higher perisomatic PV staining.
source: This lower PV innervation is comparable with E16.5 CA1PNs and contrasts with their early-born peers, the E14.5 CA1PNs, which display higher perisomatic PV staining.
evidence: This is a summary of the study's findings.

claim: According to the temporal matching rule observed in the hippocampus, E12.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons may receive preferential innervation from CA2, the earliest generated portion of the hippocampal circuit.
source: According to the temporal matching rule observed in the hippocampus (Deguchi et al., 2011), and the fact that some of them are found in the stratum radiatum and oriens, one may expect these cells to receive preferential innervation from CA2, the earliest generated portion of the hippocampal circuit (Caviness, 1973).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation with citation support.

claim: The same lower excitability (across similar metrics), combined with lower levels of PV inputs was observed in early born CA1 GABAergic neurons and DG granule cells.
source: Interestingly, the same lower excitability (across similar metrics), combined with lower levels of PV inputs was observed in early born CA1 GABAergic neurons and DG granule cells (Bocchio et al., 2020; Save et al., 2019; Gupta et al., 2012), again indicating similar fates in the adult across different subtypes of pioneer neurons.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: E12.5 CA1 pyramidal neurons may form a sparse population with multiple projections, similar to the triple projection ventral CA1 cells reported by Ciocchi and colleagues.
source: These results would suggest that E12.5 CA1PNs may form a sparse population with multiple projections, similar to the triple projection ventral CA1 cells reported by Ciocchi and colleagues (Ciocchi et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation with citation support.

claim: Triple projection ventral CA1 cells targeting the mPFC, Amy and NAcc were shown to be highly active and in particular during SWRs.
source: Interestingly, such triple projection ventral CA1 cells targeting the mPFC, Amy and NAcc were shown to be highly active and in particular during SWRs (Ciocchi et al., 2015), which would be in agreement with the fact that E12CA1 PNs receive fewer putative PV contacts.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Ventral pioneer CA1 pyramidal neurons may play a general role in the consolidation or retrieval of recent experience.
source: Based on their specific properties, we would like to propose a general role for ventral pioneer CA1PNs in the consolidation or retrieval of recent experience.
evidence: This is a speculative proposal based on the study's findings.

claim: Pioneer CA1 pyramidal neurons appear as a relatively sparse subpopulation, similar to the small minority of fast firing 'rigid' neurons.
source: Pioneer CA1PNs appear as a relatively sparse subpopulation, similar to the small minority of fast firing 'rigid' neurons (Mizuseki and Buzsáki, 2013; Grosmark and Buzsáki, 2016), however their functional role may be amplified by their various outputs.
evidence: This is a comparison with citation support.

claim: The radial subdivision of the CA1 pyramidal layer into two functional sublayers needs to be revisited by also considering the time of neurogenesis.
source: In any case, the present results indicate that the radial subdivision of the CA1 pyramidal layer into two functional sublayers needs to be revisited by also considering the time of neurogenesis.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: The initial developmental blueprint may render CA1 pyramidal neurons more resilient to diseases resulting in heterotopias and mislayering.
source: This initial blueprint may render these cells more resilient to diseases resulting in heterotopias and mislayering, as recently reported (D'Amour et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation with citation support.
